answer: Reciprocal kernel density gating. Each agent earns a kernel-weighted trust score from the spatial clustering of its transaction partners; dense reciprocal neighborhoods score high, sparse star patterns score low. New agents join only via a meadow of nearby partners whose combined scores exceed a threshold, forcing attackers to spread clones across many host clusters. A whisper channel lets neighbors flag anomalous coupling. Cost: an attacker must seed and sustain hundreds of mutually transacting identities across dispersed clusters, multiplying coordination and per-clone maintenance.
